title: Task-aligned quality adaptor and batch-significance harness for FP8/INT8 validation
creator: Sophia Patel
description:
Objective: Implement a modular metric-adaptor layer and a batch-significance harness to make accuracy validation for FP8/INT8 quantization profiles reproducible, task-aware, and CI-gatable. The adaptor layer will canonicalize model outputs across decoding modes (sampling/beam/greedy), align tokenization/detokenization differences, and expose per-task hooks for MMLU-style multiple-choice, Rouge/BLEU summarization, BLEURT/spot-check, and synthetic perplexity baselines. The batch-significance harness will measure how batching, KV-cache reuse, and variable sequence length distributions affect observable quality deltas for low-precision profiles.

Scope and deliverables:
- Metric adaptor SDK: a small runtime library (Python) that provides:
  - standardized output representation (candidates, logits, token-ids, energies, stop-positions) across model variants and generation strategies.
  - plug-in scoring adapters: perplexity-normalizer, mmlu-multi_choice_scorer, rouge_wrapper (with tokenizers used in eval-suite), bleu_wrapper, and a lightweight exact-match/extraction scorer for QA-type tasks.
  - trace metadata emission: per-sample seed, decode-mode, context-length, batch-id to feed downstream analysis.
- Batch-significance harness:
  - A benchmark runner that sweeps batch sizes (1..32), kv-cache config (on/off), and sequence-length buckets to compute per-task metric deltas and p-values using bootstrap sampling.
  - Integration with existing eval datastore (S3) and Grafana dashboard for visualization of effect sizes and significance thresholds.
- Calibration feedback loop:
  - Scripted post-processing that maps metric deltas into calibration curve inputs (delta vs scale/zero-point adjustments for INT8 and FP8 exponent ranges) and emits recommended quant-profile gates.
- CI gating rules and thresholds for canary rollouts: define per-task acceptance windows (absolute delta and relative delta), minimum sample counts and required significance level (p<0.05), and per-project weightings.

Trade-offs and design decisions considered:
- Sample-size vs cost: For heavy tasks (MMLU with 57k examples) we will use stratified sampling (task-balanced) to reduce cost while preserving power for high-variance items. Full-run will remain an option for release validation.
- Decoding-mode parity: Perplexity is only comparable under greedy log-prob computations; sampling-based outputs require calibration via temperature-adjusted baselines. We will compute both token-logprob perplexity and generation-robust scoring where applicable.
- Tokenization drift: Different model tokenizers under quantization can emit slightly different BOM/whitespace tokens leading to ROUGE/ BLEU noise. The adaptor will apply a canonical detokenization pipeline matched to the evaluation reference tokenizer.
- Metric stability vs actionable sensitivity: Avoid gating on tiny statistically significant deltas by using an effect-size floor (Cohen's d heuristic) plus business-impact weights for downstream product owners.

Acceptance criteria:
- Metric adaptor SDK published as a package (internal pip) with unit tests covering canonicalization and adapters.
- Batch-significance harness completes job matrix (batch size x kv-cache x seq-length) for at least 3 representative models and emits dashboard-ready JSON.
- Calibration mapping script produces a recommended quant-profile candidate and a summary report that ties metrics to profile changes.
- CI gating rule document and example canary config committed to infra repo.

Notes on implementation:
- Reuse existing eval runner used by ENG-6241 for ingestion and scoring. Hook adaptor as pre-processor stage.
- Use huggingface tokenizers only in the adaptor to ensure determinism across environments; include checksumed tokenizer artifacts in S3.
- Compute bootstrap significance in Rust (small crate) called from Python worker to keep runtimes low for large sample sets.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Small per-task deltas abundant but not meaningful -> Mitigate via effect-size floor and product owner signoff.
- Risk: Quantized models fail to emit compatible logits for perplexity calculation -> fall back to candidate-based scoring and mark metric as "approximate" in reports.

- Explore per-customer weighting in CI for enterprise-sensitive workloads.
